look_here_first: FIRST, FLIP A ROUND LEAF: the leaf stalk (PETIOLE) enters the UNDERSIDE AWAY FROM THE EDGE (PELTATE), with many veins radiating like an umbrella and scalloped (CRENATE) lobes. THEN FIND THE FLOWER STALK: usually a dense, many-flowered white-green terminal UMBEL-LIKE CLUSTER with many distinct flower stalklets. Whorled pennywort H. verticillata instead usually has clearly separated TIERS of a few flowers along its main stalk. Photograph the entire reproductive axis before assigning species; neither a coin-shaped leaf nor wet habitat alone is enough.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Rhizomatous perennial that roots freely at nodes, able to form stands in wet soils, ditch margins and shallow water. UT Austin Williamson flora measured foliage/flowering shoots up to about 25 cm tall.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Creeping underground to shallow exposed horizontal rhizome, often pale white, UT Williamson treatment ~1.2–1.5 mm thick with internodes ~20–60 mm and many adventitious roots at nodes.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Alternate, arising singly from rhizome nodes; no true opposite leaf pairs.

key_traits.label: Leaf
key_traits.text: Simple, orbicular/peltate disc with shallow broad crenate lobes (round scallops) and glossy green upper face; UT local 13–63 mm across; 12–16 principal veins radiate from center. Older/younger shoots vary.

key_traits.label: Petiole
key_traits.text: Long slender upright cylindrical stalk, UT Williamson account ca. 130–260 mm, white at underground base, green aboveground; attaches to lower blade surface not its margin.

key_traits.label: Leaf attachment
key_traits.text: PELTATE: junction/umbilicus is on the underside of the blade, toward its center or slightly off center. Compare Dichondra and Centella whose petiole enters an open notch at the outer blade margin.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Many tiny bisexual white to greenish-white flowers at the top of a long axillary flowering stalk. Each locally measured individual flower ~3 mm across, 5 separate star-spread petals, 5 stamens, 2 styles, and an inferior ovary. Calyx teeth/sepals absent or minute, DO NOT mislabel green structures as five leafy sepals.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Usually one many-flowered dense terminal, umbel-like cluster (botanical Williamson treatment calls the short densely packed axis a condensed raceme with 30+ helically alternate flowers) on a leafless long peduncle. Each flower on a separate pedicel; clusters ~10–15 mm across locally. A small number of additional tiers is possible: count/spacing across the full axis, not only its apex.

key_traits.label: Flowering stalk
key_traits.text: Peduncle commonly similar height to its paired leaf stalk. Pedicels spread out from compressed axis of umbel-like cluster; individually ~4–5.5 mm at anthesis in Williamson treatment, often elongating in fruit.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Small dry SCHIZOCARP of two one-seeded D-shaped MERICARPS, laterally flattened, weakly ribbed to clearly ribbed depending on maturity/light; the same UT flora reports individual mericarp ~2 × 1.4–1.6 mm. FNA/GoBotany keys note a conspicuously notched/corrugated basal contour as supporting clue versus H. verticillata. Only claim mm sizes on measured real photographs.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Moist lawn depressions, ditches, spring margins, ponds, slow margins of riparian waters, and sandy/organic saturated soils; may grow into shallow water.

key_traits.label: Season
key_traits.text: Fresh shoots and flowering are favored by adequate moisture and mild/warm weather; timing changes with rainfall, irrigation, drought and frost.

key_traits.label: Special caution
key_traits.text: Hydrocotyle umbellata is NOT a composite-headed Asteraceae, not a capsule-bearing Dichondra, and not inherently a single 'water pennywort' species: several wetland Hydrocotyle look nearly identical when sterile.
